I will discuss the synthetic approaches used to prepare these materials, their physicochemical properties and some of the challenges associated with developing effective delivery systems. The presentation will then shift from academic research to entrepreneurship, highlighting my recent experience co-founding LiT BioSciences LLC. Using this startup as an example, I will discuss the opportunities and unexpected challenges of translating scientific concepts into commercial products, including formulation development, intellectual property, manufacturing, regulatory considerations and the realities of launching a small biotechnology company. Together, these experiences illustrate how chemistry and bioengineering can contribute to innovation across multiple disciplines and how researchers can apply their scientific training to opportunities beyond the traditional academic laboratory.
